transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dan Ronan.
With just over a week until Election Day, polls suggest Republicans are losing ground
as they fight to keep control of Congress.
The final stretch of the campaign is giving both parties little time to persuade undecided
voters and get supporters to the polls.
NPR's Mar-a-Lyasyn reports.
Polls show President Trump's overall approval rating at its lowest ever, and his approval
rating on the economy in some polls is under 30%.
But the polls in the battleground House and Senate races are still very close.
In the dozen or so competitive House races, the generic ballot question, that is, would
you rather have a Democrat or Republican represent you in Congress, Democrats are ahead by only
two or three points.
And the races that will decide control of the Senate are all too close to call.
In states like Alaska, Iowa, Ohio, and Texas, polls show neither candidate ahead outside
the margin of error.
Democrats need to flip net-four seats to take the Senate majority.
Donald Trump won all those states in 2024 by double digits.
Mar-a-Lyasyn, NPR News.
Alaska's Democratic candidate for the U.S. Senate, Mary Peltova, and members of her family
were injured this weekend in a car crash while en route to a campaign event.
She sustained minor injuries requiring medical attention.
A statement said she'll be off the campaign trail until Tuesday.
Peltova is in a tight race with the incumbent Senator, Dan Sullivan.
She is attempting to become the first Democratic Senator in nearly 20 years to represent the
state of Alaska.
The Israeli army has sealed off the city of Hebron in the occupied West Bank and is forcibly
evicting Palestinians from some neighborhoods.
It comes in response to an attack by two Palestinians on an Israeli checkpoint last week.
Two soldiers died.
NPR's Ruth Sherlock reports.
Analysts say Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's decision to retaliate with such force is an
attempt to show strength as he struggles to gain a majority in the polls ahead of Tuesday's
elections in Israel.
Local authorities in Hebron in the occupied West Bank say the Israeli military has forcibly
removed more than 2,000 Palestinians from their homes.
The evictions have focused on the neighborhoods that the Palestinians who attacked the military
checkpoint came from.
The army has also placed the entire city on lockdown.
The group Physicians for Human Rights Israel says the restrictions of movement are forcing
Palestinian medical crews to transfer patients between vehicles at checkpoints and is delaying
access to hospitals.
Ruth Sherlock, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
This flag says it will install secondary seat belts on its Goliath roller coaster at its
Atlanta amusement park and on similar rides and parks it operates.
This after a 42-year-old man died two weeks ago when he was thrown from the ride.
This is NPR News.
More than 1,000 people were arrested by police in France this weekend as protesters and officers
clashed in several cities.
Police estimated more than 400,000 people took part in rallies and other demonstrations
as officers used tear gas and water cannons to break up the crowds.
The protesters are angry with the high cost of living and what they say is the need for
additional money to be spent on education.
Meanwhile, despite the protests, the National Football League today went ahead with its
first game ever played in Paris when the Pittsburgh Steelers played the New Orleans Saints.
One of the most recognizable brands in the NFL is organizing.
NPR's John Stoleness reports the Dallas Cowboy Cheerleaders now have a union.
The newly formed Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Association and the Cowboys released a joint
statement officially recognizing the new union.
The franchise said they will collectively bargain with the new union, calling the cheerleaders
an esteemed part of the Cowboys organization.
The cheerleaders' quest for better pay was chronicled in a highly popular Netflix docu-series
about the group, and following its airing, members said they worked to secure a 400 percent
pay increase for the 2025-26 season.
For years, the Cowboys faced fair-wage lawsuits from members of the cheerleading squad that
were eventually settled out of court.
One in 2019 saw a doubling of pay to $400 a game.
John Stoleness, NPR News.
Triple A says the price of gasoline and diesel remained relatively stable last week, unleaded
regular is at $428, a penny less, diesel is up two cents.
I'm Dan Roman, NPR News.

Alaska Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola injured in car crash en route to campaign event
Israeli army seals off Hebron in occupied West Bank and evicts Palestinians after checkpoint attack
